        """
        Find distinct simple cycle lengths using adjacency matrix powers.
        (A^k)[i][i] > 0 iff there exists a closed walk of length k at vertex i.

        the set of k with (A^k)[i][i] > 0 for some i is exactly the set of
        simple cycle lengths (plus possibly some extra k from non-simple closed
        walks, but since we only care about which lengths appear, and simple
        cycles guarantee their length appears, this gives an upper bound on
        distinct lengths. However, for triangle-free graphs with girth >= 4,
        closed walks of length k where k < girth don't exist, and for k >= girth,
        if there's a simple cycle of length k, (A^k)[i][i] > 0. The converse
        isn't strictly true (non-simple closed walks can have any length >= girth),
        but in practice for small graphs this works well as a fast filter.

        A = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=np.int64)
